stories.title: Washington Post ordered to rehire Karen Attiah after Charlie Kirk posts
stories.summary: Karen Attiah was fired for posts about Charlie Kirk’s assassination that the Post said violated its social media policy. An independent arbitrator has ordered the Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah and award her back pay after finding the newspaper lacked sufficient grounds to fire her. Attiah was dismissed in September 2025 following social media posts about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Attiah’s firing came amid a broader conservative campaign seeking professional consequences for people whose comments about Kirk’s assassination were deemed offensive. “This decision confirms what we’ve said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion writer, and this was wrongful termination,” Attiah said in a statement. “After spending over a decade of my career at the Post as an editor and an opinion columnist focusing on race, gender and global human rights, I’m relieved to finally have that record set straight.” The decision was issued by private arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa, according to a copy obtained by Attiah’s lawyers and cited by US media. Espinosa determined that the Post had violated its labor agreement and did not have adequate cause to terminate Attiah. “The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct,” Espinosa wrote. The dispute stemmed from posts Attiah made on Bluesky after Kirk was killed in September 2025. In one post, she referenced past comments Kirk had made about Black women. The Post subsequently said in Attiah’s termination letter that her posts breached its social media policy.

stories.title: Ex-Liverpool star Fabinho reunited with Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor
stories.summary: Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023, where he won the country’s domestic football league after his five-year stint at Liverpool. Brazil midfielder Fabinho has signed a two-year deal with Trabzonspor, the Turkish Super Lig football side has announced, and will link up with former Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah. The 32-year-old midfielder will receive a 2.6-million-euro ($3.03m) guaranteed fee and a 1.4-million-euro ($1.63m) signing fee per season, according to a Turkish stock exchange filing made by the team on Monday. “An agreement has been reached for a two-year contract with… Fabinho, who is currently in free status,” Trabzonspor posted on X. Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ittihad in 2023 and helped the team win the domestic league after his five-year stint at Liverpool. “A really special feeling to be playing with Salah again… I had the opportunity to play with him for five years in Liverpool. He is a person whom I respect a lot both for what he has done and what he will do,” Fabinho said after arriving at Trabzon airport earlier on Monday. Looking to reignite his chemistry with 34-year-old Salah, Fabinho said: “I will always try to do the best I can with whatever ability I have. “Along with the experience and leadership that come from playing for so many years, I will always try to help my teammates.” Fabinho made 219 appearances for Liverpool, helping it win the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, League Cup, Club World Cup and UEFA Super Cup titles. Egypt forward Salah joined Trabzonspor as a free agent earlier this month. Trabzonspor finished third in the Turkish top flight last season, and take on Hungary’s Ferencvaros on Thursday in the second leg of their Europa League playoff tie, trailing 1-0.
